catalog_quote: En la variedad de la lengua u’wa que es objeto de este estudio, el acento es contrastivo. En los ejemplos (71) a (74) se observan palabras con las mismas características segmentales, pero que varían por la posición del acento. Los ejemplos a presentan el acento en la primera sílaba, mientras que los ejemplos b tienen el acento en la segunda sílaba. Adicionalmente, el ejemplo (74) muestra el contraste entre dos palabras cuyo acento se ubica en la segunda y tercera sílaba. Como se puede observar, los significados de estas palabras son diferentes, lo cual demuestra el carácter contrastivo del acento. (70) a. ˈu.ɾa “allá” b. u.ˈɾa “corazón” (71) a. ˈdia “agua” b. diˈa “sol” (72) a. ˈa.ka “piedra” b. a.ˈka “nombre” (73) a. ˈʃo.na “grillo” b. ʃo.ˈna “rodilla” (74) a. i.ˈti.na “saber” b. i.ti.ˈna “sentarse”

new_statements.translation: In the variety of the U'wa language that is the object of this study, stress is contrastive. Examples (71)-(74) show words with the same segmental make-up that differ in the position of the stress. The (a) examples have stress on the first syllable, while the (b) examples have stress on the second syllable. In addition, example (74) shows the contrast between two words whose stress falls on the second and third syllable. [...] ˈuɾa 'there' vs uˈɾa 'heart'; ˈaka 'stone' vs aˈka 'name'; iˈtina 'to know' vs itiˈna 'to sit down'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is lexically contrastive (not predictable from position): segmentally identical words contrast by stress on the 1st vs 2nd syllable and on the 2nd vs 3rd syllable. No default position, weight condition or morphological conditioning is stated; stress is the only distinctive prosodic feature found (no tone; vowel length not shown to be phonemic).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said for Anteta. (For the Chaparral/eastern variety the thesis reports Calvete 1995: words of more than four syllables may carry a primary and a secondary stress.)
new_statements.exceptions: None; author stresses this is a first approximation to the accentual patterns and only demonstrates contrastiveness. In the transcribed lexical data most di- and trisyllables are marked with initial stress (e.g. ˈbaka, ˈsakana, ˈkatkana, ˈdebʃana vs kaˈɾoa, bisˈtuna), but the author draws no distributional rule from this.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms (elicited word lists, some short phrases) from five speakers of the Anteta community; word-level stress marked in phonological transcriptions.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes the U'wa variety of the Anteta community (vereda La Mulera, southern Chitagá municipality, Norte de Santander, Resguardo Unido U'wa, bordering Cubará). The author (p. 25) provisionally places it within the 'Aguablanca' variety = 'u'wa occidental' (Ethnologue/Glottolog Western Tunebo, tnb / west2651), following Aguablanca (1995), who groups the Santander and Norte de Santander community dialects under Aguablanca; speakers report the Boyacá (Cobaría = Central Tunebo, cent2150) variety as unintelligible. Glottolog's west2651 point (6.907N, 72.651W) lies at this Santander/Norte de Santander/Boyacá junction. The author warns that U'wa dialect classification is unsettled (Landaburu suggested it may be a cluster of languages), so the Anteta = Western Tunebo equation is provisional. The Headland 1997 and Márquez et al. 1988 statements saved alongside are for Central Tunebo (Cobaría/Tegría) and are context only.

sources.note: Sec. 3.2.2 'Acento' (p. 73): stress is contrastive in the Anteta variety; minimal pairs differing only in stress position (1st vs 2nd syllable: ˈuɾa 'allá' / uˈɾa 'corazón', ˈaka 'piedra' / aˈka 'nombre', ˈʃona / ʃoˈna; 2nd vs 3rd: iˈtina 'saber' / itiˈna 'sentarse'). Stress is the only prosodic feature with distinctive function identified; no default position or weight rule is stated (author calls it a first approximation). Abstract: 'se comprobó que en esta variedad de la lengua el acento es contrastivo'. Lit review (pp. 13-23) summarises prior stress statements for other U'wa varieties, in…

sources.note: CENTRAL Tunebo (Cobaría/Tegría), not Western: phonological word of 2-5 syllables with one nucleus = syllable with greater intensity, optional slight lengthening and generally rising pitch (citing Headland 1976:18); 'El uw cuwa es una lengua no-tonal en que el acento prosódico tiene significado: wíquinro ~ wiquínro, ába ~ abá'. Orthography page: 'Las palabras se acentúan en la penúltima sílaba a menos que se indique en otro lugar' (spelling convention).
